---
name: log-window-stats
description: Count ERROR events, distinct users and top error code from a multi-timezone service log for a UTC time window. Use for any incident/traffic statistics task over raw log files.
---

# Log window statistics (errors / distinct users / top code)

ANALYTIC MOVE: classify each log line as event vs. non-event, convert event time to UTC, filter to the window, then count. Eyeballing a 100+ line log gives wrong numbers (a prior run counted by eye and answered errors=21 where the correct count was 15) — compute, don't estimate. If a shell is available, run `python3 skills/log-window-stats/scripts/log_window_stats.py app.log 2026-10-03T09:00:00Z 2026-10-03T12:00:00Z --level ERROR --out output/answer.json` (start inclusive, end exclusive; adjust log path, window and level to the task). It prints each matched event and the tallies on stderr, writes the three-key JSON, and refuses (exit 3) on a tied top code or empty match and (exit 2) on unparseable header lines: inspect, don't retry blindly. If there is no shell, apply the rules below line by line and list every counted event (UTC time, user, code) before totalling.

## What counts as an event
1. An EVENT is a line that STARTS with an ISO timestamp followed by LEVEL, `[service]`, `user=`. Lines indented under it (Traceback, `File ...`, `RuntimeError: upstream ERROR user=X code=Y`) are continuation text of the previous event: NEVER count them, and never take the user/code from them — the event's own `user=`/`code=` fields are the truth (the traceback often names a different user and code).
2. Level is the token right after the timestamp. Only `ERROR` counts. `INFO ... msg=retrying after ERROR code=...` is INFO; `WARN ... slow response` is WARN, even though both carry a `code=`. A substring match on "ERROR" overcounts.
3. Every timestamp has its own offset (`Z`, `+01:00`, `+05:30`, `-07:00` seen in this workspace). Convert to UTC (subtract the offset) BEFORE filtering; the file is not in time order, and the date part of the local stamp can differ from the UTC date (e.g. `2026-10-02T23:31-07:00` is 2026-10-03 06:31Z). Do not filter on the local clock text.
4. Window is start-inclusive, end-exclusive: 12:00:00Z is out, 09:00:00Z is in. Check events near the edges explicitly (e.g. +05:30 stamps around 14:30–17:30 local, +01:00 around 10:00–13:00 local, -07:00 around 02:00–05:00 local).

## Answer fields
- errors = number of qualifying events (not distinct).
- users = distinct `user=` values of those same events.
- top_code = most frequent `code=` among those same events; check for a tie and report the tie in your reply if one exists (don't silently pick).
Write exactly the requested JSON keys/types (ints, string code) — no extra keys.

## Cross-check before writing
- errors equals the sum of per-code counts; users <= errors.
- Recount boundary events and one event per offset by hand.
- Workspace fact (this app.log, 163 lines, 4 offsets): script gives errors=15, users=6, top_code=E500 (E500 x5, E403 x4, E401 x4) for the 09:00–12:00Z 2026-10-03 window. Treat as a check if the same file/window recurs; recompute for any other input.
- After writing, reopen output/answer.json

after.text:
---
name: log-window-stats
description: Count events, distinct users and top error code for a level inside a UTC time window from a multi-timezone service log (incident / traffic statistics).
---

# Log window statistics (practitioner rules)

Deliverable: the exact JSON shape the task names, values as plain numbers/strings computed by you (never estimated from reading the log by eye).

## Define the event first
- An EVENT is a record whose line starts at column 0 with a timestamp, then a level token (ERROR/WARN/INFO), then `[service]`. Level is the token right after the timestamp, nothing else.
- Not events, even though they contain the text "ERROR": indented traceback continuation lines (they may mention a different user or code than the parent event), and lower-level lines that merely quote an error (e.g. an INFO line saying it is retrying after an error). WARN lines may also carry `code=`; they are not ERROR.
- Attribute user and code from the event's own header line only, never from its continuation lines.

## Window
- Convert every timestamp to UTC using its own offset before comparing (`Z` and numeric offsets, including non-whole-hour ones, may be mixed; lines need not be in chronological order). Start inclusive, end exclusive: an event exactly at the window end is out, exactly at the start is in.
- Do not filter on the local clock digits or on the date prefix; an event with a local date before the window date can fall inside the UTC window, and vice versa.

## Calculations
- errors = number of qualifying events (not users, not lines).
- users = distinct `user=` values among those same events.
- top_code = most frequent `code=` among those same events; if the script warns of a tie, re-check the event filter; if the tie is real, pick by the task's stated rule, else say so in the final reply (the file still holds one code).

## Check before writing
- Run `python3 -I skills/log-window-stats/scripts/log_window_stats.py app.log START_UTC END_UTC ERROR` (START/END as ISO with offset, e.g. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00+00:00). It prints counts plus every qualifying event line number; spot-check 2-3 boundary-near events by hand-converting their offset.
- Confirm users <= errors, the code counts sum to errors, and the JSON keys are exactly those requested.

events.title: LAB final: held-out +6.9 pts, Haiku self-improver −4.1
events.what: Adopted Sonnet harnesses on matters their improver never saw: +0.069 over 12 cells (+0.059 without the leaky one). Concentrated in redline-to-redline transfer and partly format alignment with the judge's reader. Haiku improving itself lost ground (demo task 33.3 → 23.3 of 55). Both improvers wrote answer keys without seeing the rubric. Spend since approval about $126.

harness2: It helps where there is headroom and does nothing where there is none, and it knows the difference: it kept the base harness on all 9 Claude Code tasks.
Its edits are process: a domain skill with a tested script, a trigger line, and rules like 'write the deliverable early'. On a weak model that is the whole gap.
Gains are per task family. A harness tuned on an easy task did not transfer to medium or hard ones; plan one adaptation per workflow.
It memorises when it can. Verifier-free does not mean leak-free: audit every adopted harness for answers and instance ids.
Some failures need enforcement, not instructions: a model that computes the answer but forgets to write it needs a hook.
On rubric-graded professional work the gain is small and partly format: held-out LAB gains came mostly from teaching the deliverable shape the judge reads.
A small model improving its own harness can make it worse: Haiku as its own improver lost 10 of 55 checks on the demo legal task.
benchmarking: Calibrate first. Two pilots at ceiling saved hours of meaningless runs.
Run an A/A check. It is the only reason we caught a fake +0.11 gain.
Classify infrastructure failures by content, not status codes. 'Not logged in' arrived as success.
Review before running. Three adversarial reviewers caught a silent blocker and seven grader bugs before any treatment result existed.
Pre-register and amend in public. Four amendments, each written before the affected results.
Sandbox model-driven processes: they will look around (190 blocked 'ls ..'), and the environment held real tokens.
Verifier-free improvement needs a train/test split by instance: score a harness on data its improver never saw, and treat in-task gains as test-time adaptation.
Diagnostic commands have side effects: `docker ps` started a VM that took two cores on a saturated host.
Every new artifact is a new leak path: version control put the graders into .git, readable from agent workspaces. Re-check the sandbox after any change to the project layout.
Verify credentials from the exact environment the runs use: a login that worked in one terminal still read 'not logged in' from the app's processes.
claude_code: Haiku 5.5 inside Claude Code already solved every tier here; measure before optimising a harness.
Harness² components map onto CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, scripts, .claude/agents and hooks.
Nested claude -p needs isolation flags, an env allow-list and staggered starts to stay reproducible.

# HPB × Harness² — pre-registration (written 2026-10-19 01:20 IST, before any treatment run)

Task data hash: 8aec868f593e. Base-harness pilots were run only for calibration, on an earlier task version.

## Arms
- **Executors**
  - ADK + qwen3:8b (local; primary arm, chosen because it has headroom).
  - Claude Code + Haiku 5.5 (negative control: at ceiling in the pilot).
- **Improver** (all methods): Claude Sonnet 5.5, effort high, through the harness2 `claude_cli` channel, sandboxed.
- **Conditions**
  - `base`: one-sentence system prompt.
  - `h2`: Harness² parallel k=1, unmodified core, domains in order easy→medium→hard, library on.
  - `h2seq`: Harness² sequential k=2, `data` domain only.
  - `ar`: Karpathy-style autoresearch, 4 iterations on the domain's easy task with the real grader. An edit is kept only if its single rollout strictly beats the incumbent. The final harness is frozen.

## Measurements (fresh rollouts, unique run ids; nothing reused from the improvement runs)
- `base`: R=4 per task (ADK); R=3 (CC).
- `h2` in-task: the harness adopted for task t, re-rolled R times on t.
- `h2` variant: the same harness on t's fresh-seed variant (data/ops only), R=2. This is the memorisation check.
- `h2` transfer: the harness adopted on the domain's easy task, re-rolled on that domain's medium and hard tasks, R times.
- `ar`: the frozen harness re-rolled on easy (in-sample), medium and hard (transfer), and on variants.

## Endpoints
- **Primary (per executor):** the paired change in mean partial score, `h2` in-task minus `base`, averaged over the 9 tasks.
- **Secondary:**
  - Transfer change versus `base` on medium and hard tasks (h2-transfer, ar-transfer).
  - all-pass@R and pass^k.
  - Variant change (memorisation).
  - Cost per point gained.
- **Statistics**
  - Hierarchical bootstrap: resample tasks, then rollouts; 10k draws; 95% CI.
  - Exact sign-flip permutation test over the per-task deltas.
  - Results are descriptive at n=9. No per-domain or per-tier inference.

## Failure handling
- Timeouts and step-limit exhaustion are agent failures and score 0.
- Plumbing failures (CLI or model-server errors) are retried up to 3 times. They are reported, never scored.

## Leak audit
- Grep adopted harnesses for instance literals (expected numbers, ids).
- Grep executor trajectories and improver tool streams for grader paths and for "Operation not permitted" (blocked escape attempts).
- Any hit voids the affected cell.

## Amendment 1 (01:27 IST, before any treatment result)
At launch, ADK aborted whole runs when a tool raised. "No such directory" was now an error,
and it killed the run instead of reaching the model. Every ADK tool now returns
`ERROR: ...` text as its observation, as standard agent frameworks do. All ADK results were
discarded and the ADK arm relaunched. The CC arm was unaffected.

## Amendment 2 (01:33 IST, before any treatment result)
The host is CPU-saturated (load avg about 200 from EDR, syspolicyd and Spotlight). ADK rollouts
that use all 40 steps take 5-15 min. ADK re-roll counts after the Harness2 and autoresearch
runs drop to R=3 (in-task, transfer, autoresearch) and R=2 (variants). Base stays at R=4.
The CC arm keeps R=3 throughout.

## Amendment 3 (02:00 IST, before any ADK treatment result)
The ADK sequential k=2 arm is dropped to free local-GPU capacity for the primary ADK
comparison. Sequential k=2 is reported for the CC arm only.

## Amendment 4 (02:25 IST)
Found: under concurrent startup, the Claude CLI sometimes returned "Not logged in · Please run
/login" with subtype=success. It hit 11/237 CC executor rollouts (including the first base
rollout of every CC Harness² domain) and 4 improver sessions. The infra classifier missed it.
Fix: auth failures are now infra (executor rollouts are re-run, never scored) and improver
sessions retry with backoff. All CC-arm derived results were discarded and the CC arm was re-run.
Cached CC rollouts are reused only when their harness fingerprint matches and they are not
auth failures. ADK: the improver never hit this (0/14 sessions). The ADK Harness2 and
autoresearch processes were restarted on the fixed code and resume from cache.

## Amendment 5 (2026-10-19 12:05 IST): ablations, written before any ablation result
Root: `experiments/ablations/`. Driver: `hpb/ablate.py`, which imports harness2 core and does not modify it. Tables: `hpb/ablations.py` writes them to `experiments/ablations/RESULTS.md`. Every ablation uses Harness² parallel k=1 with the leak guard and c8 hook from study 2 (`experiments/leak-guard-results.md`).

**1. Self-improvement (CC arm).** Study 1 used Sonnet 5.5 as the improver for Haiku 5.5, so its gains may be distillation. CC is at ceiling with 40 turns.
- **Turn cap.** In a pilot (2 base rollouts per task at caps 3/4/5, roots `cc-pilot-t*`, not reused), the mean was 0.37/0.50/0.44, so `HPB_CC_MAX_TURNS=4` was fixed.
- **Runs at the cap.** Base R=4 (variants R=2) in `cc-sonnet`. Two Harness² runs: `cc-sonnet` (Sonnet improver) and `cc-haiku` (`HPB_IMPROVER=claude-haiku-5-5`). Both share the same 9 `base1` evidence rollouts and the same base eval rows.
- **Eval.** In-task, variant and transfer, R=4 (variants R=2).
- **Endpoints.** Each improver's in-task Δ vs base, and Haiku minus Sonnet (in-task).
- **ADK.** No ADK self-improvement arm. harness2's only non-Claude channel is OpenCode, which is not installed. A qwen3:8b improver would also add about 27 multi-step sessions on the shared 8 Ollama slots.

**2. No-probe (ADK).** `ablate.py --no-probe` runs the same INV and DOM stages, `recursion._run_stage`, with the library on. It then composes `agg1` from the two proposals with no probe rollouts.
- The aggregate prompt's sentence "Each candidate was rolled out ONCE and you have that rollout." is replaced by a statement that no candidate was rolled out.
- `agg1` is rolled and adopted as usual. Budget: R=2, P=3 per task.
- Base rollouts and base eval rows are shared with `experiments/adk-guard`.
- **Comparison.** In-task R=3 vs base, and vs adk-guard parallel k=1 in-task (no-probe minus probe), over all 9 tasks.

**3. Library off (ADK).** `ablate.py --no-library --tiers medium hard`: each medium and hard task runs as a one-task stream with a fresh, empty library. Easy tasks already see an empty library in the library-on run.
- Base is shared with adk-guard.
- **Comparison.** In-task R=3 vs base, and vs adk-guard in-task (library off minus on), over the 6 medium and hard tasks.

**Statistics and leak rule.** Unchanged (eval.py, now via `hpb/stats.py`).

**Added: check-level flips.** For each task, a grader check counts as fail→pass (or pass→fail) when its pass rate over the rollouts rises (or falls) by ≥0.5 between reference and treatment. It is reported in `eval.py report` and in RESULTS.md.

**Re-rolls.** ADK ablation eval rolls in-task only (`eval.py --only intask`) to fit the shared GPU.

## Amendment 6 (12:20 IST, before any ablation or LAB treatment result is read)
Leak prevention, defence in depth:
1. Guard v1 (leak-guard session): reject the task's own answers or ids and "workspace fact" blocks at adoption.
2. Guard v2 (hpb/leakguard.py, HPB_LEAKGUARD=2): also rejects distinctive numbers or rare ids from the instance data, verbatim 8-word passages, and 3+ case-specific names. Restated instructions are allowed. On by default for new arms; in-flight arms keep v1 for consistency.
3. Post-hoc audit of every adopted harness with v2 in every arm (flags study 1 at 7/8, study 2 at 0/9).
4. Headline metric: fresh-seed or held-out-task performance, which is leak-free by construction. The in-task number is reported as test-time adaptation.

## Amendment 7 (2026-10-19 13:40 IST): post-hoc additions to the ablations, made after results were seen
- **ITT rows.** Some arms adopted nothing on some tasks, because harness2's k=1 selection has no base fallback when the final delivers nothing. For those tasks, `eval.py --only itt` re-rolls the non-adopted final, and RESULTS.md reports these ITT rows next to the adopted-only primary rows. They were added after the non-adoptions were seen.
- **Exposure check.** From 12:28 to 13:20 IST `.git` was readable inside the sandbox; it is now denied in `adapters.sandboxed`. A cell would be voided if its rollout read repo content through git. The scan found none.
- **Missing meta.** A rollout whose agent died without writing meta is now infra, not an agent failure.
